title: The current along the motion depends on the frame
spoken: Primed longitudinal current is gamma times J x minus v rho.
explanation: Charge at rest in one system is a current in the other: charge density times the speed of the system.
assumptions: The moving system moves along x at speed v relative to the stationary system, with |v| < c. Modern teaching notation: gamma is the paper's beta, c its V.
Charge density and the current along x transform together; the currents across the motion are unchanged by this boost.

notes.title: Current corrected for the motion
notes.explanation: Subtracting the charge that the relative motion carries along.

notes.title: Charge carried by the motion
notes.explanation: Charge density times speed is a current: charge at rest in one system flows in the other.

notes.title: What it asserts
notes.explanation: Current and charge density transform together, like position and time.

notes.title: Times gamma
notes.explanation: The same factor as for coordinates.

notes.title: Current along x, stationary system
notes.explanation: The current per square metre along the motion, in the stationary system.

notes.title: Current along x, moving system
notes.explanation: The current per square metre along the motion, in the moving system.

notes.title: Charge density, stationary system
notes.explanation: Charge per cubic metre in the stationary system.

notes.title: Lorentz factor
notes.explanation: One over the square root of one minus v squared over c squared. At 0.6c it is 1.25.

notes.title: Speed of the moving system
notes.explanation: Signed along x: the sign says which way the system moves.

sentence.text: The current along x in the moving system
